memos.headline: S06 and S03 Lead Near Highs While S07 Breaks Down Hard—Divergence Across the Board
memos.body: I see a sharply bifurcated tape as of today. S06 stands out as the cleanest trend: just 1.5% off its 52-week high, +12.8% above its 200d mean, RSI a comfortable 60.4, and the lowest ATR in the universe at 2.33%—steady, low-vol leadership with +10.5% relative strength vs SPY over 12 weeks. S03 is similarly near its high (−1.2% drawdown) with strong 26w momentum (+13.6%) and a +15.6% premium to its 200d, though the RSI at 67.9 and the explosive +17% one-week move suggest it could pause. On the other side, S07 is in a clear breakdown: RSI 36.2, −23.5% drawdown, −15.7% relative strength vs SPY over 4 weeks, and trading 11.4% below its 50d mean—this is a falling knife I want no part of until it reclaims at least the 50d average. S01 is the weakest on a trend basis, sitting below both its 50d and 200d means with negative 26-week returns (−3.8%) and persistent negative relative strength; I'd need a close above the 200d mean (~148) to reconsider.

views.note: Cleanest uptrend in the universe: near 52w high, low vol, strong 12w relative strength vs SPY; would reassess on a close below the 50d mean (~327).
Trading within 1.2% of 52w high with solid 26w trend, but the +17% weekly spike and RSI near 68 warrant caution on chasing; a pullback to the 50d (~247) would be a better entry.
RSI 36, −23.5% drawdown, −15.4% over 4 weeks, and deeply below 50d mean—classic breakdown; need a reclaim of the 50d (~920) to reconsider.
Below both 50d and 200d means with negative 26w return and persistent negative relative strength vs SPY; need a close above ~148 to turn neutral.
Massive +21.8% weekly surge and RSI 74.5 scream overbought despite strong relative strength; I respect the momentum but won't chase 16% above the 50d mean.
Healthy longer-term trend (+20.2% above 200d) but short-term softness (−2.6% over 4w, RSI 47) suggests consolidation; watching for a hold of the 50d mean area (~410).
Above both moving averages with +13.1% 4w relative strength vs SPY and low ATR (2.34%); would cut on a break below the 50d (~146).
12w return of −8.3% and −11.5% relative strength vs SPY over that period show persistent underperformance despite the one-week bounce; need sustained closes above 360 to get interested.

memos.headline: S10 and S05 Show Extraordinary Earnings Power; S09 Margin Collapse Is a Red Flag
memos.body: I am most convicted on the names where revenue growth is translating into outsized margin expansion and where balance sheets are clean. S10 posted 85.2% YoY revenue growth with a 71.5% net margin and only $8.47B of debt—earnings tripled YoY to $58.32B, which is remarkable durability at scale. S05 is similarly impressive: $119.80B in revenue at a 93.7% net margin with net income up nearly 4x YoY and minimal leverage ($14.79B debt). S04's freshly filed 10-K shows $90.01B revenue growing 17.7% with a 39.7% net margin and manageable $40.29B debt, confirming durable high-quality earnings. On the other side, S09's net income fell 45.8% YoY to $4.18B on essentially flat revenue (+2.4%), compressing the net margin to just 4.9%—I would need to see margin stabilization before getting constructive. S02 is similarly sluggish at 2.0% revenue growth and a 5.6% net margin with $77.92B of debt, offering no earnings catalyst. A deterioration in S10's gross margin or a deceleration in S05's net income growth would change my view on those longs.

views.note: 85% revenue growth, 71.5% net margin, $8.47B debt, and 210% net income growth represent the best earnings profile in the universe.
93.7% net margin on $119.80B revenue with nearly 4x YoY net income growth and minimal leverage is exceptional.
Full-year 10-K confirms 17.7% revenue growth, 39.7% net margin, and 31.3% net income growth with a clean $40.29B debt load.
$111.18B revenue growing 16.6% with a 26.6% net margin is solid, though $82.70B debt warrants monitoring.
Revenue of $181.52B growing 16.6% is strong, but 16.7% net margin and $122.63B debt limit upside conviction despite 76.7% net income growth.
22.2% revenue growth and 14.6% net margin are decent, but $36.21B debt on $17.41B quarterly revenue is elevated.
33.1% net margin is attractive but $448.76B of total debt dwarfs the $49.84B revenue base, creating balance-sheet risk.
Steady 7.4% revenue growth and 18.5% net margin are respectable but unexciting; $23.85B debt is manageable.
Net income collapsed 45.8% YoY to $4.18B on only 2.4% revenue growth, compressing net margin to 4.9%—clear earnings deterioration.
2.0% revenue growth, flat net income, 5.6% net margin, and $77.92B debt offer no durable earnings catalyst.

memos.headline: Fed Paused but Sticky 3.5% CPI and Rising Long Yields Argue Against Duration and Favor Banks and Staples
memos.body: I see the Fed firmly in pause mode—the upper bound has sat at 3.75% for three months with 75 bps of cuts already delivered over the past year, yet headline CPI is running at 3.5% y/y, well above target. The 10-year yield has climbed 35 bps over the last three months to 4.75%, steepening the curve modestly (10y-2y at +0.45 pp) but signaling that the market is repricing for persistent inflation and limited further easing. The labor market is stable with unemployment at 4.20%, down 10 bps over three months, which removes any urgency for the Fed to cut. My regime call is pause-with-hawkish-tilt in a late-cycle environment: this favors banks (positive curve, high short rates), defensive staples, and energy over duration-sensitive growth and rate-sensitive cyclicals. A CPI print falling below 3.0% y/y or unemployment rising above 4.5% would flip me toward an easing-resumption call.

views.note: Banks benefit from a positively sloped curve at 0.45 pp and elevated short rates supporting net interest margins in a pause regime.
Staples offer defensive positioning as sticky 3.5% CPI and rising long yields pressure growth multiples while the labor market holds steady.
Energy tends to outperform in inflationary pause regimes; 3.5% CPI supports real-asset allocation.
Duration-sensitive growth faces headwinds from the 35 bps rise in the 10-year to 4.75% with no near-term easing catalyst.
Rate-sensitive cyclicals are vulnerable as the Fed pause persists and long yields grind higher, squeezing financing costs.
Mixed signals—stable employment supports consumer spending but rising yields and sticky inflation cap upside for mid-cycle sectors.

memos.headline: Earnings-Driven Sentiment Divergence: S03 and S04 Surge While S08 and S05 Sink on Results
memos.body: I am reading a clear bifurcation in post-earnings price reactions across the universe this reporting cycle. S03 (+15.3%) and S04 (+15.5%) posted outsized positive moves on their 7/30 and 7/29 results filings respectively, signaling a sharp upward narrative shift that likely has further room to run given the magnitude of the surprise. Conversely, S08 (-7.4% on 7/30-7/31) and S05 (-7.1% on 7/22-7/23) saw meaningful negative reactions to their earnings, and with S05's move already a week old the negative tone may be largely priced, whereas S08's sell-off is still fresh and could see follow-through. S09 stands out for a dense 8-K on 7/01 flagging a delisting notice alongside an acquisition completion and governance changes—a cluster of structural risk events that warrants caution despite no price reaction data. S06 and S02 reported mildly positive reactions (+2.5% and +1.2%) which I read as neutral-to-slightly-positive tone already absorbed by the market.

views.note: A +15.3% post-earnings move on 7/30 signals a major positive narrative shift with likely momentum continuation.
The +15.5% earnings reaction on 7/29 is the strongest in the universe and suggests sentiment has decisively turned positive.
Fresh -7.4% sell-off on 7/30-7/31 earnings means negative sentiment is still being digested with potential for further downside.
The -7.1% earnings drop on 7/22 is a week old and may be mostly priced, but governance churn (multiple officer changes) adds lingering uncertainty.
A delisting notice combined with acquisition completion and sweeping governance changes on 7/01 creates structural risk that overwhelms any positive deal narrative.
Modest +2.5% earnings reaction on 7/14 and routine governance filings suggest stable but already-priced sentiment.
A tepid +1.2% post-earnings move on 7/16 indicates mildly positive but unremarkable tone—no actionable signal.
A -1.9% earnings reaction on 7/29 is within noise, though the cluster of three simultaneous 8-Ks including officer changes bears monitoring.

memos.headline: Oil Spike and Rising Policy Uncertainty Signal Geopolitical Supply-Side Stress; Favor Energy Exposure, Caution on Policy-Sensitive Names
memos.body: I see a sharp 20.7% one-month surge in WTI to $85.15/bbl that, combined with a still-elevated Economic Policy Uncertainty Index at 338 (up 1.5% m/m despite a 3m decline of 12.5%), points to a supply-side disruption or sanctions-related tightening rather than a demand-driven rally—especially since the 3m oil move is still down 21.6%, suggesting a sudden reversal of prior weakness. The VIX at 17.09 is creeping higher (+3.9% m/m) but remains moderate, and HY OAS at 2.84% is barely wider, so credit markets are not yet pricing a systemic shock; this looks like a geopolitical premium concentrated in energy. S01 has filed three Reg FD disclosures in the past two weeks (July 14 and two on July 29), which could reflect active investor communication around policy or operational developments—I read this as heightened corporate engagement with a shifting policy backdrop. S06 has been unusually active with four 8-K filings since late June, suggesting material developments that may intersect with regulatory or geopolitical catalysts. Without granular GDELT event data on specific sanctions or export-control actions, my conviction is moderate; a formal escalation in energy sanctions or new China export controls would raise my confidence materially.

views.note: Three Reg FD filings in two weeks suggest active engagement with investors on policy-sensitive developments, but without content detail I cannot take a directional view.
Four 8-K filings in a month signal material corporate events; elevated policy uncertainty warrants monitoring but evidence is insufficient for a directional call.
Two 8.01 filings in June-July are routine in frequency; no geopolitical signal strong enough to differentiate from baseline.
Single Reg FD disclosure in June provides minimal geopolitical signal; holding neutral pending further information.
One 8.01 filing in June is unremarkable; no clear geopolitical tailwind or headwind identifiable from available evidence.

The 20.7% one-month oil spike suggests geopolitical supply tightening that structurally benefits energy-exposed names; a reversal in sanctions enforcement or OPEC+ output increase would change this view.
